messages:
Alex Park: Heads-up — Eversafe Bank wants to replace GiantAPI with Redwood for our hosted inference. They care most about deterministic parity for their regulatory chatflows, KMS/HSM integration, and a smooth pricing migration. Can we map ask -> blocker?
Priya Sen: Thanks. They're running ~8k concurrent chats at peak, mostly short sessions (avg 80 tokens). Primary asks: 1) response parity w/ GiantAPI for a set of 120 prompts, 2) legal/security Qs for KMS and data residency, 3) how pricing transitions from GiantAPI flat-contract to per-token / reserved capacity.
Alex Park: @Priya yes. Also they invoked a hard requirement: no behavioural regressions on 10 canned prompts used for AML screening. They want canary rollout and automatic fallback to legacy provider during parity window.
Javier M.: For parity: we should capture request/response differences first. Two quick questions: how do they call GiantAPI today? sample header?
Priya Sen: They use header Authorization: Bearer GIANT-KEY, content-type application/json with streaming disabled. Example payload: {
  "model":"giant-chat-v1",
  "input":"<user prompt>",
  "max_tokens":150,
  "temperature":0.0
}
Priya Sen: They also use a custom top_p shim and post-process some tokens client-side.
Li Chen: Temperature 0.0 helps parity. Key issues we see migrating are: tokenization differences, detokenized probability ties, and function-calling signatures. We can add a compatibility shim to normalize tokens and enforce deterministic sampling.
Nora Simmons: Security checklist: KMS integration, HSM support, SAG logging controls, audit trails, and ability to disable model telemetry. Eversafe requires FIPS 140-2 for key storage and monthly audit logs retention for 7 years.
Mark R.: Legal note — they want contract language for dual-provider fallback and breach notification SLA subclauses. Will need redlining.
Alex Park: Actionable asks for eng: parity run of their 120-prompt suite, recommend config for deterministic matching, and a canary plan with fallback behavior. Also cost estimate for hybrid months (30% traffic to Redwood, 70% legacy) plus reserved capacity options.
Javier M.: I can run a quick parity harness. Can we get the 120 prompts + expected outputs? Prefer them in a CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_text. Also tell us whether they expect exact token-level match or semantic equivalence.
Priya Sen: I'll ask them to upload CSV to the secure bucket. They want exact matches for 40 of the prompts and semantic parity for the rest.
Li Chen: Proposed runtime tweaks for parity: quantization profile locked to q4_0 for that model family, tokenization shim to use GiantAPI's BPE offsets, and deterministic sampling: temperature=0, top_p=0.95 + seed. We can also expose a compat flag: compat_mode=giantapi_v1 to replicate function-calling wire format.
Nora Simmons: On KMS: we support AWS KMS and a customer HSM via PKCS#11 connector in Private mode. For Hosted, we can offer tenant-controlled keys in a dedicated CMK. Need SOC2 and third-party pen test dates.
Alex Park: Pricing ask: they want a transition plan: first 3 months hybrid with per-token pricing discounted to match legacy blended price, then commit to Dedicated after month 3. Who owns the numbers?
Mark R.: Finance and sales can draft a blended quote. Legal needs to review the hybrid billing language, especially around overages and credits when fallback triggers.
Priya Sen: Next steps I propose: 1) Eversafe uploads CSV + sample request logs (sanitized) by EOD Wed. 2) @javier and @li run parity harness and share quick delta report within 48h. 3) @nora to send security artifact list (SOC2, pen test, FIPS notes) and KMS options. 4) Sales to draft blended quote and canary SLA.
Javier M.: Ack — I'll provision an isolated test harness and run 120 prompts. Will include token-diff report and suggested shim code snippet.
ops-bot: deploy:parity-harness started by javier — build #482 queued (link: https://ci.redwood.ai/482).
Li Chen: Example shim snippet I'll drop in report:
```
// normalize tokens to GiantAPI BPE
const normalized = tokenizeAsGiant(prompt);
const resp = await redwood.generate({ model: 'rw-compat-v1', prompt: normalized, temperature:0 });
return detokenizeToOriginal(resp.tokens);
```
Priya Sen: Great — keep the customer looped. I'll schedule a tech-PoC call Thurs 4pm PT to walk them through canary and fallback mechanics.
Alex Park: Thanks team — please post the parity report + delta artifacts in the thread when ready and flag any non-starters. :thumbsup:
